title: ARMMAN: AI-Enabled Support for High-Risk Pregnancy Care
short_description: WhatsApp-based AI assistant supported ANMs with real-time clinical guidance, strengthening high-risk pregnancy management statewide.
long_description: ARMMAN (Keyword: Frontline Health Worker Support) Keywords: Frontline Health Worker Support, Maternal Health, Neonatal Health, AI, WhatsApp Chatbot, High-Risk Pregnancy, Clinical Decision Support, Multilingual, Voice-Based, Human-in-the-Loop, Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives, Continuous Learning, Protocol-Aligned Guidance Organization: ARMMAN Mission: Reducing preventable maternal and child mortality by addressing delays in care-seeking and gaps in frontline health worker training. Scale: Rolled out to 1,000 ANMs in Uttar Pradesh, pilot with 50 ANMs in Telangana, serving 2,00,000+ pregnant women. Challenge: High-risk pregnancies account for 20-30% of all pregnancies in India but contribute to 70-80% of maternal and neonatal deaths, largely due to poor early identification and management. Frontline health workers, particularly Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives (ANMs), are overburdened, undertrained, and lack timely, context-specific guidance. Infrequent trainings and digital fatigue from using 6-8 different government applications further hinder effective care and clinical decision-making. Solution: ARMMAN developed a multilingual, multimodal AI assistant for Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives, delivered via WhatsApp. The solution provides real-time, protocol-aligned clinical guidance, doubt resolution, and bite-sized learning, supported by a human-in-the-loop escalation pathway to ensure safety, accuracy, and contextual relevance. Key Technologies: WhatsApp-Based AI Assistant: Instant, protocol-aligned clinical guidance embedded in existing workflows. Multilingual & Multimodal Support: Text and audio interactions for accessibility. Human-in-the-Loop Escalation: Safety oversight for complex or out-of-scope queries, handling 19% of cases. Validated Medical Protocols: Grounded in evidence-based antenatal care practices. Bite-Sized Continuous Learning: Embedded into day-to-day practice without added burden. Impact: The AI-enabled assistant has improved frontline confidence with high engagement and scalable clinical support. With deployment to 1,000 ANMs in Uttar Pradesh and 50 ANMs in Telangana serving 2,00,000+ pregnant women, 70% of ANMs have asked at least one question and 85% of activated users have returned for a second conversation. The system has handled over 12,000 real clinical queries with 98% positive user feedback and 97% of responses rated satisfactory by domain experts. The solution resolved approximately 80% of queries without trainer intervention, reducing trainer workload and the need for refresher sessions. Learnings for Others: Supporting Decisions at the Point of Care: Embedding protocol-aligned support within WhatsApp enabled real-time assistance within existing workflows. Scaling with Clinical Safeguards: Human-in-the-loop escalation ensured safety while allowing the solution to scale effectively. Learning Embedded in Daily Practice: Bite-sized learning integrated into routine interactions enabled continuous capacity building without added burden.
keyword: Frontline Health Worker Support, Maternal Health, AI

title: Adalat AI: AI-Enabled Courtroom Operations Accelerating Justice Delivery
short_description: AI courtroom operating system automated transcription and documentation, significantly speeding case processing and improving judicial efficiency.
long_description: Adalat AI (Keyword: Justice Delivery) Keywords: Justice Delivery, Judicial Efficiency, AI, Legal Tech, Courtroom Automation, Speech-to-Text, Real-Time Transcription, Case Management, Natural Language Processing, Legal Large Language Models, Multilingual, India, Global South, Digital Transformation Organization: Adalat AI Mission: Building an end-to-end AI platform for courts in India and the Global South to modernise courtroom workflows and make justice delivery more timely, efficient, and accessible. Scale: Working directly with High Courts and District Courts across India, addressing the challenge of over 50 million pending cases nationwide. Challenge: India's judiciary faces over 50 million pending cases, with an average case taking nearly 13 years to conclude. Manual documentation processes and chronic shortages of stenographers created severe bottlenecks. Courts spent disproportionate time on routine tasks such as dictation, order writing, and evidence summarisation, limiting judicial capacity for adjudication. This severely impacted litigants, particularly those from low-income and marginalised communities. Solution: Adalat AI built an AI-powered courtroom operating system that enables real-time transcription, automated documentation, and streamlined case-flow management within courtrooms. Optimised for Indian legal language and multilingual proceedings, the platform reduces manual workload for judges and court staff, accelerates hearings, and strengthens the efficiency of justice delivery. Key Technologies: Live Speech-to-Text Transcription: High-accuracy transcription optimised for Indian accents, dialects, and legal vocabulary with speaker attribution. Natural Language Processing: For understanding legal context and terminology. Legal Large Language Models: Custom models for automated generation of orders, judgments, and case notes. Multilingual Translation: Between English and major Indian languages for proceedings. Case-Flow Management Dashboards: For judges and court staff to track progress. Searchable Repositories: For transcripts and evidence with easy retrieval. Secure Deployment: On-premise or sovereign cloud options meeting judicial data standards. Impact: The AI-powered courtroom system has fundamentally accelerated justice delivery. Kerala mandated Adalat AI for evidence recording, marking the first statewide AI mandate in courts globally. Order-writing time was reduced from 45-60 minutes to under 10 minutes, and courts are now able to examine 2-3× more witnesses per day. Judges reported 30-50% quicker case disposal in matters using AI-generated documentation, with significant reduction in reliance on stenographers, addressing a long-standing systemic constraint in the judicial system. Learnings for Others: Automation Unlocks Judicial Capacity: Reducing time spent on routine documentation enabled judges to focus more on adjudication, accelerating hearings and case disposal. Embedding AI into Core Workflows Drives Adoption: Deploying AI directly inside courtrooms, rather than as a peripheral tool, supported sustained use by judges and staff. Trust and Security Are Non-Negotiable: Privacy-preserving models and sovereign deployment options were essential for institutional acceptance in the justice system.

title: Civic Innovation Foundation: Digitising Public Consultation for Democratic Governance
short_description: AI platform scaled public consultations nationwide, enabling governments to incorporate citizen input into stronger, more inclusive policies.
long_description: Civic Innovation Foundation (Keyword: Civic Engagement) Keywords: Civic Engagement, Democratic Governance, AI, Public Consultation, Policy-Making, Governance, Pan India, Digital Transformation, Citizen Participation, Transparency, Multilingual, Voice-Based Feedback, RAG, NER Organization: Civic Innovation Foundation (CIVIS) Mission: Enabling structured, inclusive dialogue between governments and citizens on draft laws and policies. Scale: Conducted 1,250+ public consultations reaching 8,24,306 citizens across 777+ cities and towns, pan-India. Challenge: Public consultation mechanisms relied on fragmented and manual processes such as emails and written submissions. Governments struggled to manage large volumes of unstructured feedback, ensure inclusive participation across literacy levels and languages, and translate citizen inputs into actionable policy insights. This limited the effectiveness and credibility of consultations and weakened democratic participation. Solution: CIVIS developed an AI-enabled, end-to-end public consultation platform that supports governments across the consultation lifecycle. The platform enables structured citizen engagement, multi-channel and multilingual feedback collection, and advanced analysis of qualitative inputs to translate public feedback into actionable policy insights. Key Technologies: AI-based Policy Draft Analyser: Uses Named Entity Recognition (NER) and clause-mapping to break down draft laws into understandable components. Response Analyser with RAG Pipeline: Synthesises large volumes of feedback using Retrieval-Augmented Generation with reranking. Whisper v3: Transcribes multilingual voice inputs including WhatsApp voice notes. Llama 3.1: Open-source large language model for reasoning and summarisation. Moderation Tools: Ensures safe, relevant, and policy-focused engagement. Dashboards & Reports: Provides structured insights, trends, and summaries of public sentiment. Impact: The AI-enabled consultation platform has fundamentally strengthened both reach and effectiveness of public consultations. With over 8,24,306 citizens engaged across 1,250+ consultations, between 32% and 76% of citizen feedback has been incorporated into draft laws and policies. More than 3,000 hours of multilingual voice feedback has been analysed, lowering barriers for citizens. The platform supported 40+ government partners, with notable impact in 2024 when proposed amendments to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules were paused after feedback highlighted implementation challenges. Learnings for Others: Human-Centred AI Design: Voice-first, multilingual engagement ensures inclusion without compromising analytical rigour. Scalability with Trust: Open-source models and transparent workflows build credibility with government partners. From Participation to Influence: Structured analysis and clear reporting closes the loop between citizen input and policy decisions.

title: SEEDS: AI for Resilient Cities: Hyperlocal Risk Mapping for Inclusive Climate Action
short_description: AI-powered hyperlocal risk mapping helped cities predict climate hazards accurately and prioritise protection for vulnerable households.
long_description: SEEDS - Sustainable Environment and Ecological Development Society (Keyword: Climate Resilience) Keywords: Climate Resilience, Disaster Risk Reduction, AI, Climate Adaptation, Hyperlocal Mapping, Predictive Analytics, Flood Risk, Heat Risk, Cyclone Risk, Urban Vulnerable Communities, Satellite Imagery, GIS, Machine Learning, Community-Led Solutions Organization: SEEDS (Sustainable Environment and Ecological Development Society) Mission: Protecting lives and livelihoods through community-led, resilience-based solutions. Scale: Reached approximately 1,00,000 families across 10 cities including Delhi, Nagpur, Chennai, and Bhubaneswar across India and Asia. Challenge: India faces increasing climate and disaster risks from heatwaves, floods, cyclones, and earthquakes, disproportionately affecting people in informal settlements. Disaster planning remained reactive and lacked granular, real-time data, making it difficult to identify the most vulnerable households and take early, targeted action. Existing planning relied on city- or ward-level averages, obscuring household-level vulnerability and limiting effective resource allocation. Solution: SEEDS developed an AI-driven, hyperlocal risk mapping system that integrates satellite imagery, geospatial layers, environmental indicators, and household data to generate building-level, multi-hazard vulnerability scores. The system enables governments and communities to anticipate risks, prioritise interventions, and implement preventive, community-led resilience measures. Key Technologies: Satellite Imagery & Land-Use Data: For building footprints, roof types, and vegetation cover. Meteorological & Time-Series Climate Data: For forecasting and risk prediction. Spatial Analysis & Supervised Learning: For generating hyperlocal vulnerability scores. Multi-Hazard Forecasting Models: Predicting heat, floods, cyclones, and earthquakes. Interactive GIS Dashboards: Supporting planners and field teams with actionable insights. Adaptive Learning Loops: Integrating sensor data and community feedback to refine assessments. Impact: The AI-driven risk mapping platform has enabled a shift from prediction to prevention with measurable resilience outcomes. Reaching approximately 1,00,000 families across 10 cities, the system achieved 85-88% accuracy in identifying multi-hazard risks and enabled insulation of 1,650+ high-risk homes, reducing indoor temperatures by 8-12°C. title: The Apprentice Project: AI-Powered 21st Century Skills At Scale
short_description: AI-powered WhatsApp learning platform enabled large-scale 21st-century skills development with measurable gains in creativity and problem-solving.
long_description: The Apprentice Project - TAP (Keyword: 21st Century Skills) Keywords: 21st Century Skills, Education, AI, Critical Thinking, Problem-Solving, Creativity, Decision-Making, WhatsApp Learning, Adaptive Learning, EdTech, Public Schools, Personalised Learning, Multimodal AI, Computer Vision, Assessment, NEP 2020, STEM, Coding, Financial Literacy Organization: The Apprentice Project (TAP) Mission: Embedding 21st-century skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and decision-making into India's public education system. Scale: Enrolled 100,000 children with 3,000+ trained teachers, delivering choice-based co-curricular learning pathways for students in Grades 4-12 across public schools. Challenge: India's public education system serves over 250 million children, yet 21st-century skills critical for a digital economy remain largely untaught and unmeasured. Overcrowded classrooms, exam-driven pedagogy, limited teacher training, and one-size-fits-all instruction restricted opportunities for personalised learning. Skills such as creativity, problem-solving, and decision-making were neither systematically developed nor assessed at scale, with no structured curricula, assessment frameworks, or real-time data on skill progression. Solution: TAP developed TAP Buddy, an AI-powered WhatsApp learning platform that delivers personalised, adaptive skill development directly to students. Using multimodal AI, rubric-based evaluation, and real-time feedback, the solution enables continuous measurement and learning while strengthening teacher capacity through dashboards, guidance, and system-level insights. Key Technologies: Conversational AI: For interactive learning embedded in WhatsApp. Personalised Adaptive Learning Engine: Adjusting difficulty and pacing based on student performance. Computer Vision: AI-based evaluation of visual projects and assignments. Voice Evaluation: Assessment of audio submissions against rubrics. LLM-Driven Doubt Resolution: For students and teachers to get instant answers. Interactive Micro-Learning Videos: With in-video comprehension checks. Behavioural Nudges: To improve engagement and retention. Predictive Analytics: Alerts for disengagement and low mastery. Dashboards: For teachers, schools, and governments to track progress. Impact: The AI-powered learning platform has demonstrated scalable, low-cost skills learning with measurable outcomes. With 100,000 students enrolled and 61% active usage, the system achieved average weekly mastery levels of 54-65% across coding, science, and financial literacy. Significant skill growth was measured from baseline to endline: creativity improved by 42.6%, problem-solving by 50.8%, and decision-making by 43.5% over 6-8 months. Delivery was achieved at ₹800 per child, projected to reduce to approximately ₹100 per child annually at scale, demonstrating cost efficiency and sustainability for government adoption. Learnings for Others: Personalisation Enables Scale: Adaptive learning paths allowed diverse learners to progress at their own pace, leading to measurable skill gains across large cohorts. Multimodal Assessment Makes Skills Measurable: AI-based evaluation of projects and explanations enabled continuous measurement of complex skills at scale that were previously difficult to assess. Low-Cost Design Enables Sustainability: A WhatsApp-first, reusable-content model kept per-child costs low, supporting long-term government adoption and scalability.

title: Udhyam Learning Foundation: Udhyam Saathi – AI Mentor
short_description: AI mentor provided personalised project support to students and teachers, increasing engagement, iteration, and curriculum adherence.
long_description: Udhyam Learning Foundation (Keyword: Entrepreneurial Mindsets) Keywords: Entrepreneurial Mindsets, Education, AI, AI Mentorship, Project-Based Learning, Experiential Learning, WhatsApp, Multilingual, Rubric-Based Feedback, Teacher Support, Government Schools, Youth Development, 21st Century Skills, Scale Organization: Udhyam Learning Foundation Mission: Building agency and entrepreneurial mindsets at scale through a four-year Entrepreneurial Mindset Curriculum (EMC) for students and teachers in government schools. Scale: Rolled out to 8 lakh students and 30,000 teachers across 6 states, with overall program reaching 3.9 million students across 12 states. Challenge: Udhyam's Entrepreneurial Mindset Curriculum reaches millions of students through experiential, project-based learning. At scale, however, teachers faced a mentorship bottleneck and were unable to provide timely, personalised, and domain-specific feedback on student projects. This resulted in incomplete work, limited iteration, uneven learning outcomes, and high administrative burden on teachers, constraining the effectiveness of learning by doing and creating inequitable access to quality mentorship across geographies. Solution: Udhyam Saathi is an AI-powered mentor designed to deliver equitable, continuous support to students and teachers at scale. For students, it functions as a 24/7 mentor answering project queries in multiple languages, evaluating ideas, prototypes, and pitches, and providing personalised, rubric-based feedback that supports iterative learning. For teachers, it serves as an AI co-pilot, automating reviews, resolving curriculum queries, and tracking student progress to enable more focused, high-quality coaching. Key Technologies: Multilingual Multimodal AI Mentor: Delivered primarily through WhatsApp with Progressive Web App support. 24/7 Query Resolution: Instant responses to student questions with personalised feedback. Evaluation System: Assessment of submissions across text, image, and video formats. Rubric-Based Assessment: For ideas, prototypes, and pitches aligned to learning objectives. AI Co-Pilot for Teachers: Curriculum guidance, automated reviews, and progress tracking. Dashboards: For monitoring student progress and program impact. Guardrails & Validation: Query pre-processing, relevance checks, and prompt safeguards including Negative Test Suite. Privacy & Security: PII masking, authorisation-based access, SSL-secured APIs. Impact: The AI-enabled mentorship platform has improved engagement, adherence, and learning quality at scale. Expanding access to 8 lakh students and 30,000 teachers across 6 states, the system achieved 85% of teams submitting milestones (9% increase) and 97% submitting two project ideas (versus 51% last year). Approximately 10% of teams revised submissions based on AI feedback. Student submissions showed dramatic improvements: 59.5% increase in ideas per team, 163% increase in novelty of ideas, and 126% improvement in articulation. Overall project quality is expected to improve by approximately 50% year-on-year. Learnings for Others: Extending Mentorship Unlocks Engagement: AI-based mentoring addressed teacher capacity constraints and ensured timely, personalised feedback, leading to higher participation. Meeting Users Where They Are Drives Adoption: Delivering mentorship through WhatsApp reduced friction and enabled sustained usage and rapid scaling. Feedback Enables Iterative Learning: Rubric-based, timely feedback encouraged students to revise and improve their work, contributing to higher curriculum adherence and improved project quality.

title: Vowels of the People Association (VOPA): AI & Evidence-based FLN Assessments
short_description: AI-driven FLN assessments revealed real learning levels, prompting statewide action to strengthen foundational literacy and numeracy.
long_description: Vowels of the People Association - VOPA (Keyword: Education Assessment) Keywords: Education Assessment, Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, FLN, AI, Automatic Speech Recognition, ASR, Evidence-Based Assessment, Education Technology, EdTech, Maharashtra, Oral Reading Assessment, Real-Time Analytics, Teacher Training, Policy Impact, Scale Organization: Vowels of the People Association (VOPA) Mission: Building technology-led, scalable solutions in education and mental health to nurture responsible and empowered citizens. Scale: Assessed approximately 16 lakh students statewide through the 'NIPUN Maharashtra' app, mobilising 6,000 education supervisors for 66,000 school visits. Challenge: Official FLN assessment data in Maharashtra indicated reading proficiency levels of 69-74%. However, evidence-backed assessments revealed actual proficiency below 40%, with nearly 60% of early-grade children struggling with basic reading and numeracy. Existing assessment practices relied on superficial or rote-based evaluations, creating false visibility, delaying interventions, and leading to misinformed policy and resource allocation decisions worth hundreds of crores. Solution: VOPA developed an AI-powered FLN assessment system through the 'NIPUN Maharashtra' app to deliver accurate, joyful, and scalable oral reading and numeracy assessments. The solution enables real-time, evidence-led evaluation using speech recognition, adaptive assessment flows, and automated reporting, with role-specific dashboards for all stakeholders. Key Technologies: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR): Refined open-source Marathi Indic AI models for oral reading assessment. AI-Driven Oral Reading & Numeracy Assessments: Across alphabets, words, sentences, and passages. Real-Time Audio Streaming: With noise detection and chunking for low-bandwidth classrooms. Automated Assessment Reports: Capturing words per minute, accuracy, and error patterns. Role-Based Dashboards: For teachers, headmasters, supervisors, and administrators. Government System Integration: With UDISE+, SARAL, and SHALARTH platforms. Impact: The AI-powered assessment system has revealed reality, reshaped priorities, and enabled evidence-led action at scale. Assessing approximately 16 lakh students statewide and mobilising 6,000 education supervisors for 66,000 school visits, the system showed only 39% reading proficiency versus 69% previously reported, triggering a statewide reset of FLN priorities. This evidence influenced teacher training plans, departmental budgets, and monitoring frameworks worth hundreds of crores. The solution provided granular insights on reading speed, accuracy, and error patterns, enabling targeted interventions by grade and geography, with 1,87,000+ app downloads and positive feedback from over 1,300 teachers and education officers. Learnings for Others: Evidence Unlocks Action: Replacing inflated assessments with AI-backed evidence revealed true FLN gaps, enabling the state to reset priorities and redirect training, monitoring, and budgets at scale. Designing for Scale Enables Adoption: Simple, joyful, and low-friction assessment flows allowed quick adoption, supporting statewide rollout and coverage beyond targets. Data Strengthens Accountability: Granular, role-based dashboards linked outcomes to action at every level, improving follow-through and enabling targeted interventions.

title: William J Clinton Foundation: AI-enabled Express Health Camps
short_description: AI-enabled health camps used portable X-rays for rapid TB screening, detecting cases earlier and reducing screening time and cost.
long_description: William J Clinton Foundation - WJCF (Keyword: TB Detection) Keywords: TB Detection, Public Health, AI, Chest X-Ray, Active Case Finding, Healthcare, Tuberculosis, Radiology, Computer Vision, Offline-First Technology, Government Partnership, Community Screening, Early Detection, Health Systems Strengthening Organization: William J. Clinton Foundation (WJCF) Mission: Supporting government-led health systems to reduce disease burden and save lives across TB, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, and non-communicable diseases. Scale: Works across 16 states with Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and state governments, screening 12,12,932 beneficiaries through AI-enabled Express Health Camps. Challenge: India bears 26% of the global TB burden, yet traditional symptom-based screening fails to detect a large proportion of cases. Limited availability of radiologists (approximately 20,500 serving 1.4 billion people, or 15 per million), poor care-seeking behaviour (63% of individuals with chest symptoms did not seek care), and reliance on manual workflows constrained the effectiveness of community-based Active Case Finding, resulting in missed diagnoses and delayed treatment. 42.6% of TB confirmations would have been missed without chest X-rays. Solution: WJCF deployed an AI-enabled Express Health Camp model using ultraportable chest X-ray devices integrated with an offline-first Radiological Information System (RIS). The system enabled instant AI-driven interpretation, beneficiary data capture, and triage at the point of screening without reliance on internet connectivity, allowing large-scale, efficient TB detection in low-resource settings. Key Technologies: Ultraportable Chest X-Ray Devices: For community-based screening in field settings. AI Interpretation Engine: Instant, automated analysis of chest X-ray images. Offline-First Radiological Information System (RIS): Modular, vendor-agnostic system for data capture and storage. Beneficiary Data Management: Capturing demographics and screening information. Role-Based Access Control: Ensuring smooth field operations across teams. Instant Triage System: Enabling immediate referral and follow-up for positive cases. Dashboards & Reports: For program teams to track coverage and outcomes. Impact: The AI-enabled screening system has transformed TB detection efficiency and outcomes at scale. Deployed across 72 machines nationwide, the system screened 12,12,932 beneficiaries and confirmed 9,804 TB cases, including 32% asymptomatic cases often missed by symptom-based approaches. Screening time per beneficiary was reduced from 8-10 minutes to under 3 minutes, achieving a 62% reduction in screening time and cost. The Number Needed to Screen (NNS) was 127 for one TB confirmation, with average screening cost reduced to approximately INR 1.5 per beneficiary. Learnings for Others: Offline-First Systems Enable Reliable Screening: Designing for low-connectivity settings directly increased coverage in resource-constrained areas. AI-Led Triage Reduces Dependence on Scarce Resources: Reducing reliance on radiologists accelerated confirmations and improved detection rates. Integrating AI into Routine Workflows: Embedding AI into existing government screening workflows lowered costs while improving yield and detection outcomes.

title: demo design case Study
short_description: WhatsApp-based AI assistant supported ANMs with real-time clinical guidance, strengthening high-risk pregnancy management statewide.
long_description: ARMMAN (Keyword: Frontline Health Worker Support) Keywords: Frontline Health Worker Support, Maternal Health, Neonatal Health, AI, WhatsApp Chatbot, High-Risk Pregnancy, Clinical Decision Support, Multilingual, Voice-Based, Human-in-the-Loop, Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives, Continuous Learning, Protocol-Aligned Guidance Organization: ARMMAN Mission: Reducing preventable maternal and child mortality by addressing delays in care-seeking and gaps in frontline health worker training. Scale: Rolled out to 1,000 ANMs in Uttar Pradesh, pilot with 50 ANMs in Telangana, serving 2,00,000+ pregnant women. Challenge: High-risk pregnancies account for 20-30% of all pregnancies in India but contribute to 70-80% of maternal and neonatal deaths, largely due to poor early identification and management. Frontline health workers, particularly Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives (ANMs), are overburdened, undertrained, and lack timely, context-specific guidance. Infrequent trainings and digital fatigue from using 6-8 different government applications further hinder effective care and clinical decision-making. Solution: ARMMAN developed a multilingual, multimodal AI assistant for Auxiliary Nurse-Midwives, delivered via WhatsApp. The solution provides real-time, protocol-aligned clinical guidance, doubt resolution, and bite-sized learning, supported by a human-in-the-loop escalation pathway to ensure safety, accuracy, and contextual relevance. Key Technologies: WhatsApp-Based AI Assistant: Instant, protocol-aligned clinical guidance embedded in existing workflows. Multilingual & Multimodal Support: Text and audio interactions for accessibility. Human-in-the-Loop Escalation: Safety oversight for complex or out-of-scope queries, handling 19% of cases. Validated Medical Protocols: Grounded in evidence-based antenatal care practices. Bite-Sized Continuous Learning: Embedded into day-to-day practice without added burden. Impact: The AI-enabled assistant has improved frontline confidence with high engagement and scalable clinical support. With deployment to 1,000 ANMs in Uttar Pradesh and 50 ANMs in Telangana serving 2,00,000+ pregnant women, 70% of ANMs have asked at least one question and 85% of activated users have returned for a second conversation. The system has handled over 12,000 real clinical queries with 98% positive user feedback and 97% of responses rated satisfactory by domain experts. The solution resolved approximately 80% of queries without trainer intervention, reducing trainer workload and the need for refresher sessions. Learnings for Others: Supporting Decisions at the Point of Care: Embedding protocol-aligned support within WhatsApp enabled real-time assistance within existing workflows. Scaling with Clinical Safeguards: Human-in-the-loop escalation ensured safety while allowing the solution to scale effectively. Learning Embedded in Daily Practice: Bite-sized learning integrated into routine interactions enabled continuous capacity building without added burden.
keyword: Frontline Health Worker Support, Maternal Health, AI
